slides: Open with the chapter's warning: orbit spaces are easy to name and hard to trust. The lecture is about the hypotheses that turn an orbit set into a smooth manifold, then about the standard constructions that reuse the quotient mechanism.

Use the dependency graph as the proof traffic map. Freeness controls isotropy, properness controls topology, and together they lead to embedded orbits, adapted charts, and the quotient manifold theorem. The check verifies paths from both freeness and properness to the theorem.

This gallery is the diagnostic slide. Horizontal translations give a clean one-dimensional quotient, rotations of the plane fail freeness at the origin, irrational torus flows fail properness through dense orbits, and lattice translations give a good torus quotient.

Properness prevents escaping group elements from producing convergent points and images. The dilation sequence has group elements running to 34 while points tend to zero and images stay at one, showing nonproper behavior. The irrational torus return errors decrease toward zero, revealing near-returns rather than separated orbits.

The adapted chart is the local theorem picture. In coordinates (x,y), the orbit direction is x and the quotient coordinate is y, so the quotient map becomes (x,y) to y. The projection Jacobian has rank one, matching dim M minus dim G in the model.

Discrete free proper actions are the covering-space case of quotient manifolds. For the Z squared action on the plane, a small radius 0.18 patch has nontrivial translates at distance at least one, so nearby sheets stay disjoint. In a five-by-five window, the displayed fiber has 25 representatives.

Homogeneous spaces are quotients by isotropy. A transitive action identifies the whole space with G/H after choosing one base point. The SO(n)/SO(n-1) model gives spheres, and the dimension check matches n minus one across the sampled values.

Lie quotient groups reuse the same theorem with normal closed subgroups. The covering homomorphism t to exp(2*pi*i*t) has integer kernel samples and tiny invariance residual. The QR connectivity check keeps a path inside GL plus by maintaining positive determinant.

The applied lab is a decision table, not a proof substitute. For each candidate action, check smoothness, freeness, properness, the expected quotient, and whether the theorem applies. The failed cases name the obstruction: fixed origin for freeness, dense orbits for properness.

Close by making the theorem portable. A useful quotient manifold needs more than an open quotient map: freeness removes isotropy, properness separates orbit classes, adapted charts supply local coordinates, and the same template explains coverings, homogeneous spaces, quotient Lie groups, and connectedness applications.
